correctness.rationale: Verified both the frozen formulas and the narrowed repair. Tensor projectors give four bands, only the middle two of which can collide, and four positive detector weights. The permanent dark complement is orthogonal, invariant and loss-free; the four-band sector has precisely one simple real root at resonance because any real eigenvector must be detector-orthogonal and simultaneously an eigenvector of the unperturbed operator. Thus the sitewise absorption drop is the squared overlap with the normalized middle-band dark vector. For the linewidth, independently write y=z-E_2, let E_1-E_2=delta and denote the two middle weights by u=(n-1)/(mn), v=(m-1)/(mn), with W=u+v. Rank-one expansion of the characteristic determinant gives W y-v delta=(2i/gamma-F)y(y-delta), where F is the real-at-resonance sum of the two noncolliding resolvent terms. Its derivative in y at the collision is W>0. The first-order root is y=v delta/W, so Im y=-2uv delta^2/(gamma W^3)+O(|delta|^3), yielding the asserted population factor of 4. The slow spectral projection tends to the orthogonal detector-null middle vector projection, which has squared site overlap D, and the permanent dark complement contributes 1-Q. A fixed fast-spectrum contour strictly below the real axis bounds the remaining propagator uniformly for both signs of sufficiently small detuning, including at repeated fast roots. This proves the t=s/delta^2 limit for s>0. All conclusions hold at fixed finite m,n>=2 and positive beta,gamma, without assuming any nonnormal eigenbasis or running source scripts.
residual_risks: The limit is not uniform as the graph grows or detector strength tends to zero or infinity; it is not the instantaneous t=0 survival.

evidence: The rectangular theorem gives both the asymptotic capture of every input and the rank (1+min(r,m-1))(1+min(s,n-1))-epsilon, hence rank four or three in the singleton case; its finding is an infinite-time capture theorem.

For the same rank-one sink, Razzoli et al. use Krylov reduction. Their strongly regular evaluation covers the equal-hopping 3-by-3 rook graph, with parameters (9,4,1,2) and probability 1/4 from every nontrap vertex.

The strongly regular calculation neither retains the arbitrary anisotropy nor supplies the approach rate.

value.rationale: The narrowed finding moves beyond known eventual capture and the generic existence of dark states: the explicit positive coefficient sets a lifetime across all finite board sizes, while the crossover identifies exactly how much probability persists for each source at that time scale. Together the prefactor, detector-strength dependence and site weights quantify a genuine singular transport limit that cannot be learned from the old rank drop. The narrow dynamical result is worthwhile on its own.
residual_risks: No claim of broader detector geometry, new general perturbation technique or new static law remains.
